comments.text:
Actually the full context of this part in history was that the French started the Panama Canal project in 1881 and stopped in 1887 when French company who was buulding the canal went bankrupt. Which is then America bought all the french equipment, excavations, and property rights in 1904. 

The Hay-Herrán Treaty in 1903 would had granted the U.S. a lease on the canal zone in exchange for cash payment and annual rent. The Columbian Governornment didn’t take the deal cause they figured the financial payments was too low to give up a strip of their territory. And Columbia knew that the French company was going bankrupt and so all of their equipment would revert back to Columbian control and then they would sell it to the U.S. for a higher price.

The Panamanian people, frustrated by Columbia refusal, revolted. Protected by the U.S. with gunship diplomacy, as shown in the short, delcared independence and signed the Hay-Bunau-Varilla Treaty, granting the U.S. permanent control over the canal zone.

My personal opinion is that Columbia lost both territory and financial windfall cause they were too greedy.
